title: observability-pipeline-debug-notes-wip-2
content:
High-level context:
- Started seeing sporadic metric drops and trace gaps for the hosted-api ingest pipeline in us-west-2 around 2025-11-15 02:30 UTC. Symptoms: 10-30% of traces show missing span sets for post-inference enrichment step; metrics_count for 'model.request.count' down ~18% for 30s windows, then recovers. Logs show repeated 5xx from enrichment service (enricher-v2) and occasional S3 read timeouts from cache loader.

What I observed so far (timeline):
- 2025-11-15 02:28 UTC: alert firing for metric-drop-runbook (pager duty).
- 02:30-02:45 UTC: multiple retries from ingestion-proxy; circuit-breaker tripped briefly for enricher shards 3 & 4.
- 03:00 UTC: manual rollback of enricher-v2 -> enricher-v2-prev reduced error rate but didn't fully restore metrics.
- 03:20 UTC: spikes in kinesis-lag on route 'hosted-api->ingest' correlated with increased batching latency.

Repro steps attempted (local + cluster):
1) Replayed a controlled 5k req trace volume against staging ingest (same routing rules) - could reproduce traces missing post-enrich spans ~2% of time.
2) Ran curl to ingestion-proxy hitting /ingest with large payloads (50KB) - observed 504s from enricher occasionally.
3) Javaclient instrumentation dump: confirmed that agent attaches spans but downstream enrichment RPC sometimes returns early with ECONNRESET.
4) Pulled logs for enricher pods across nodes 12-17 between 02:20-03:10 UTC: see repeated "cache loader timed out after 120s" and stack traces pointing to s3-sdk GetObject timeouts.

Key error snippets from logs: (redacted)
- enricher-v2[2025-11-15T02:33:14Z] ERROR: CacheLoader - failed to pull key model-features/abc123 from s3: request timed out after 120000ms
- enricher-v2[2025-11-15T02:33:15Z] WARN: RPCClient - retry 3/5 to ingestion-proxy due to ECONNRESET
- ingestion-proxy[2025-11-15T02:34:01Z] ERROR: Dispatcher - downstream enricher shard=4 returned 502 Bad Gateway
- kinesis-consumer[2025-11-15T02:35:10Z] ERROR: CommitLoop - failed to flush window: backpressure threshold exceeded

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Intermittent S3/GCS regional latency causing cache loader timeouts -> enricher blocks -> requests queue up -> circuit-breaker trips -> traces drop. Evidence: s3 timeouts in logs, correlation with kinesis lag spikes.
2) Network flakiness on nodes hosting enricher shards (EC2 instance networking issue) causing TCP resets -> 502/504. Evidence: ECONNRESET in RPC logs; affected pods concentrated on nodes 12-17.
3) Regression in enricher-v2 introducing synchronous blocking on cache miss path (120s timeout) that wasn't present in v2-prev. Evidence: rollback reduced errors but not fully; stack traces include new code paths for blocking fetch.

Commands and queries I ran: (useful for replay)
- kubectl -n prod logs enricher-v2-5fd8c -c cache-loader --since=1h | grep -i timeout | sed -n '1,200p'
- kubectl -n prod describe pod enricher-v2-5fd8c | egrep 'Node:|Image:|Restart'
- aws s3api list-objects --bucket redwood-cache-prod --prefix model-features/ --query 'length(Contents)'
- aws cloudwatch get-metric-statistics --namespace "Redwood/Storage" --metric-name "RequestLatency" --start-time 2025-11-15T02:00:00Z --end-time 2025-11-15T04:00:00Z --period 60 --statistics Average
- curl -v -X POST "https://ingest.redwood.com/ingest" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '@sample-request.json' --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 15

Observability/trace snippets to inspect:
- trace_id: 2f8a4e9b-... (sample) shows span sequence: client->proxy->router->ingestion-proxy->{enricher call missing post-enrich span}
- trace_id: 8c1d9f0a-... shows RPC to enricher returns 502 then retry path includes "fast-fail" tag.

Temporary mitigations tried:
- Rolled enricher-v2 -> enricher-v2-prev on 3 nodes (partial) -> error rate decreased ~60% on those nodes.
- Increased cache-loader timeout from 120s -> 240s in k8s config (hotfix) -> reduced S3 timeout logs but increased headroom for queueing (still seeing kinesis-lag).
- Added a resilience rule in dispatcher: reduce max concurrent requests to enricher from 300 -> 150 per shard to reduce tail latency.

Next steps / experiments to run:
- Coordinate with infra/networking to check node-level NIC errors for nodes 12-17 (dmesg, ENA errors). Ticketed infra: JIRA-OBS-1193 (network node health).
- Re-run load replay after fully rolling back enricher-v2 in a canary subset; compare trace coverage and span completeness.
- Run S3 perf tests from the same AZs as affected nodes to measure tail latency (simple get-object microbenchmark, measure p99).
- Instrument additional logging in cache-loader: include X-Request-Id, backoff/window position, and which S3 endpoint was used (dual-stack?).
- Consider switching to async non-blocking cache fetch for v2 if regression confirmed.

Notes / learnings:
- Partial rollback helped, which points to code-path regression or configuration change in v2, but S3 timeouts and node concentration mean multiple factors likely amplifying issue.
- Need better correlation between kinesis lag and s3 latency metrics (currently stored in separate dashboards). Plan to add a combined dashboard for ingest path with trace coverage % by time window.

Open questions: 
- Are there any infra changes (OS/kernel/AMI) deployed to nodes 12-17 in the 24h before the incident?
- Did we change S3 endpoint routing (VPC endpoints) or presigned-url libraries in last release?
- Could regional S3 control plane incidents have started around 2025-11-15? (check AWS health dashboard)

Quick checklist to triage (for on-call):
- [ ] Check CloudWatch S3 latency p50/p95/p99 for redwood-cache-prod across regions
- [ ] Check node NIC errors (dmesg) for nodes hosting enricher shards
- [ ] Validate enricher v2 config - especially cache timeouts and blocking flags
- [ ] If problem persists, rollback enricher-v2 fully for affected AZ and monitor trace completeness

Attachments / artifacts to add to ticket: sample-trace-2f8a4e9b.json, enricher-v2-log-snippet-02-33.txt, kinesis-lag-graph-20251115.png

Personal TODO (follow-up):
- Add unit/integration test for non-blocking cache fetch path in enricher next sprint.
- Schedule 30m sync with infra + release-engineering to review node patching history.
- Clean up temporary hotfix (240s timeout) once root cause identified.

If anyone picks this up: start with the "cache loader" logs and node dmesg for nodes 12-17, then validate S3 latency from the AZ. Ping me in slack @jamie with pointers to traces you find.
